instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic, slice the scallions and chop the cilantro. Cut the bok choy in half lengthways.
Divide the garlic, scallions, cilantro, both soy sauces, the vinegar and the salt between 4 large heatproof bowls.
Cook the noodles in the boiling water as the package says. Add the bok choy for the last 2 minutes.
Drain well and divide the noodles and bok choy between the bowls, setting them on top of the seasonings.
Put the pepper flakes on the adults' bowls only, 1/2 tsp on each.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan over high heat for about 2 minutes, until it shimmers and a pinch of scallion sizzles right away. Stand back a little. It will spatter.
Carefully pour the hot oil over the bowls a little at a time, so each one gets about the same. It will sizzle loudly.
Toss each bowl so the noodles pick up the seasonings.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Cup of Yum (the lead, 4.9 from 40) and The Woks of Life (4.87 from 22) agree on the whole method: noodles and greens in a bowl over soy sauces, vinegar, garlic and scallions, then hot oil poured over. SBS's version is bigger on vinegar and uses peanut oil; this uses plain vegetable oil to keep it nut-free and a middle amount of vinegar. The sources scale for one serving, so amounts are multiplied for four. Buy egg-free noodles. The chili flakes go only on the adults' bowls to keep the base mild.
